title: Protocol and Contact
premise: Yara Dunmore, a former signals analyst living under four assumed identities, is jolted out of hiding when a dead colleague's voiceprint unlocks a black-site server in Lisbon containing proof of the sanctioned operation that killed civilians—and Yara's own recorded testimony, which someone has been shopping to the highest bidder. Hunted by both the agency that wants him silenced and a private broker who wants the archive intact, Yara must decide whether to destroy the evidence or deliver it to a journalist whose motives he can't verify. In the end, Yara trades the one secret worth killing for—the location of a second witness—to buy passage on the dawn extraction flight, sacrificing his chance at vindication but finally sleeping through the night as the plane lifts off.
about_author: Ansel Sandoval is the pen name of a former compliance auditor who spent six years documenting institutional cover-ups before turning to fiction. He writes from three different cities and admits to none of them.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Living as 'Martin Hale' in a coastal town, Yara catalogs his nightly rituals of vigilance—bolt checks, burner rotations, the 3 a.m. startle. A routine grocery run nearly exposes him when an old agency phrase is spoken aloud behind him. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of permanent invisibility, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. An encrypted message arrives using the voiceprint of Tomas Reyes—dead for two years. Following embedded instructions, Yara remotely triggers a dormant server in Lisbon; its index shows his own testimony file, timestamped last month. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past isn't buried, it's been circulating without him.

chapters.title: Hale Is a Dead Man
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Yara burns the 'Hale' identity in four hours: cash withdrawal patterns, apartment stripped, car abandoned at a ferry terminal. He watches from a hillside as two men in a gray sedan canvass his street. Emotional beat: grief for a life that was only ever scaffolding.

chapters.title: What Reyes Left Behind
chapters.summary: POV: Yara, with flashback fragments in Reyes's voice. Deciphering Reyes's dead-drop protocol, Yara learns the server holds full operational logs of the Vantaa incident—and that Reyes didn't die accidentally. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse Marchetti (the broker). Ilse, who has been auctioning access to the archive, contacts Yara through a cutout: deliver the decryption key, receive money and a clean identity—or she sells his location to the agency. Emotional beat: cold professionalism masking her own leverage problem.

chapters.title: Night Train to Rotterdam
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Moving by rail under a fifth name, Yara notices a tail who is too good—counter-surveillance habits he recognizes because he trained them. He loses the man in a station crowd but finds a tracking device sewn into his own coat lining. Emotional beat: paranoia curdling into the realization that someone inside his old circle is hunting him personally.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Waits
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia Okafor. Investigative journalist Nadia Okafor, holding half the Vantaa story for two years, receives a signal that the other half exists. She weighs publishing against the source protection failures that killed her last collaborator. Emotional beat: principled hunger shadowed by fear of repeating a fatal mistake.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Using Reyes's tradecraft, Yara initiates contact with Nadia through layered cutouts. Their first exchange is terse, mutually suspicious, and precise—he tests her, she tests him back. Emotional beat: the fragile, almost tender mechanics of trust between strangers.

chapters.title: Agency Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV: Deputy Director Corliss. Corliss learns the archive is live and orders containment, quietly authorizing 'disposition' of all linked persons—including, if necessary, the retrieval team itself. Emotional beat: bureaucratic evil rendered as calendar management.

chapters.title: The Second Witness
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Decrypting a fragment, Yara discovers Reyes hid a second witness—Priya Nair, the incident's surviving comms officer—in a safehouse outside Porto. The realization lands: the key isn't just evidence, it's a person's address. Emotional beat: the weight of holding someone else's life in a cipher.

chapters.title: Ilse Moves First
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. Unable to locate Yara directly, Ilse feeds the agency a partial trail to force him toward her, then travels to Porto on a hunch about the second witness. Emotional beat: ambition colliding with the first flicker of conscience.

chapters.title: Porto Rain
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Yara reaches Priya ahead of everyone—but she refuses to move, traumatized and convinced extraction is how Reyes died. Their standoff breaks when the safehouse's motion sensors trip. Emotional beat: fear transmuted, briefly, into solidarity.

chapters.title: Safehouse Siege
chapters.summary: POV: Priya. Agency operators breach the safehouse; Yara and Priya escape through a drainage culvert while Ilse, arriving mid-raid, photographs the team's faces instead of stopping them—a pivot point. Emotional beat: terror, adrenaline, and the strange intimacy of shared flight.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Cornered by Ilse in a hotel stairwell, Yara negotiates: she gets exclusive first publication rights via Nadia; he gets her extraction contact and the flight manifest for a dawn departure. Emotional beat: wary alliance built on mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: Corliss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: POV: Corliss. With the raid failed, Corliss locks down airports and burns a favor to get the extraction pilot's schedule—then realizes Ilse now holds photos implicating his own operators. Emotional beat: control slipping into damage limitation.

chapters.title: Nadia's Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia. Offered the complete archive, Nadia must publish immediately—blowing every cover—or hold it and risk the sources dying overnight. She schedules release for the moment wheels leave the runway. Emotional beat: the loneliness of deciding alone.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. The extraction contact demands the one thing Yara withheld: Priya's current location, as insurance against double-cross. Yara faces trading a witness's safety for his own exit. Emotional beat: moral nadir—the arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: What Yara Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Yara gives the contact a poisoned version of the location—a decoy safehouse wired with Reyes's old countermeasures—keeping the real one memorized nowhere but his head. Emotional beat: reclaiming agency; justice outside the law means writing your own terms.

chapters.title: Airport Chess
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Yara/Corliss. A pre-dawn cat-and-mouse across terminals: Corliss's watchers, Ilse's insurance play, Nadia's countdown clock. Yara slips the net by moving as airport staff, badge forged from Hale's old skills. Emotional beat: coiled, breath-held tension.

chapters.title: Dawn Runway
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. On the tarmac, the extraction plane idles; Corliss's last operator confronts Yara, and Ilse—choosing publication over payment—intervenes with her photographs as leverage. Yara boards as the archive goes live worldwide. Emotional beat: climax—release after suffocation.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Witnessed
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia. The story detonates; Corliss is suspended pending inquiry, operators named, hearings announced. Nadia protects Priya's new identity and declines to confirm whether Yara was ever a real person. Emotional beat: vindication that feels incomplete without its author.

chapters.title: One Name, Finally His Own
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Somewhere over open water, Yara fills in a landing card with a fifth name—not an alias this time, but one he chose himself. He sleeps before the seatbelt sign goes off. Emotional beat: resolution—identity reclaimed not by erasing the past but by carrying it deliberately.
